originalTitle: U.S. stock futures tick higher as soft jobs data eases Fed hike bets
summary: Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures edged up on Sunday evening after Wall Street closed higher on Friday, as weaker-than-expected jobs data reduced expectations for another Federal Reserve interest-rate hike this month, while elevated Treasury yields and oil prices limited gains.
content:
Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures edged up on Sunday evening after Wall Street closed higher on Friday, as weaker-than-expected jobs data reduced expectations for another Federal Reserve interest-rate hike this month, while elevated Treasury yields and oil prices limited gains.

S&P 500 Futures inched 0.1% higher to 7,784.0 points, while Nasdaq 100 Futures rose 0.3% to 31,148.0 points by 20:06 ET (00:06 GMT). Dow Jones Futures traded 0.1% higher at 51,513.0 points.

Stocks ended Friday's session higher after the Labor Department reported that U.S. employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, well below economists' expectations for a 90,000 increase.

The unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, while August payroll growth was revised lower to 133,000 from 162,000.

The data prompted traders to scale back expectations for a Fed rate increase at the central bank's upcoming meeting. Markets were pricing in roughly an 80% probability that the Fed would leave rates unchanged this month, according to CME FedWatch.

Not finding the right stocks? Our AI's list of investor-grade stock picks for October just dropped »

The softer labor market has supported rate-sensitive technology shares. On Friday, the NASDAQ Composite rose 1.2%, while the S&P 500 gained 0.7% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.5%,

Still, gains in U.S. equities face pressure from a renewed selloff in government bonds and persistent concerns about energy-driven inflation.

Treasury yields initially fell after the jobs report but later reversed higher, as investors remained wary that elevated oil prices could keep inflation above the Fed's comfort zone.

Oil prices remain a key risk for markets as the conflict involving Iran continues to disrupt energy supplies. Brent crude has traded above $100 a barrel, while the prospect of prolonged disruptions has kept inflation concerns elevated.

The energy market's inflationary impact could complicate the Fed's policy outlook even as the labor market shows signs of cooling.

Investors will also focus on the start of the third-quarter earnings season, with corporate results likely to test whether elevated borrowing costs and energy prices are weighing on profit expectations.

chineseContent:
Investing.com——周五华尔街收高后，美国股指期货周日晚间小幅上涨，原因是就业数据弱于预期，降低了美联储本月再次加息的预期，而国债收益率和油价上涨限制了涨幅。

截至美国东部时间 20:06（格林威治标准时间 00:06），标准普尔 500 指数期货上涨 0.1%，至 7,784.0 点，而纳斯达克 100 期货上涨 0.3%，至 31,148.0 点。道琼斯期货上涨 0.1%，至 51,513.0 点。

周五股市收高，此前美国劳工部报告称，美国雇主 9 月份仅增加了 29,000 个就业岗位，远低于经济学家预期的 90,000 个增量。

失业率从 4.1% 升至 4.2%，8 月份就业人数增幅从 162,000 人下调至 133,000 人。

该数据促使交易员降低了对美联储即将召开的会议上加息的预期。根据 CME FedWatch 的数据，市场预计美联储本月维持利率不变的可能性约为 80%。

劳动力市场疲软支撑了对利率敏感的科技股。周五，纳斯达克综合指数上涨 1.2%，标准普尔 500 指数上涨 0.7%，道琼斯工业平均指数上涨 0.5%，

尽管如此，美国股市的上涨仍面临政府债券再度抛售以及对能源驱动型通胀持续担忧的压力。

就业报告公布后，美国国债收益率最初下跌，但后来反转走高，因为投资者仍担心油价上涨可能使通胀率高于美联储的舒适区。

由于涉及伊朗的冲突继续扰乱能源供应，油价仍然是市场的主要风险。布伦特原油价格已突破每桶 100 美元，而长期供应中断的前景令通胀担忧加剧。

尽管劳动力市场显示出降温迹象，但能源市场的通胀影响可能会使美联储的政策前景变得复杂。

投资者还将关注第三季度财报季的开始，企业业绩可能会检验借贷成本和能源价格上涨是否会影响利润预期。
